one_line_contribution: A measurement instrument rather than a method: the substitution ratio S, quantifying how much of an ExpeL-style experience bank's benefit survives once a reflective prompt optimizer (GEPA) is given exactly the same training episodes, paired with a frozen whole-bank-compiled instruction arm that tests whether per-instance retrieval buys anything at all, and a near-duplicate positive-control bank that is supposed to make a null interpretable.
closest_prior_work: Two uncited works threaten this more than anything in the proposal's related-work section. (1) Agent Workflow Memory (arXiv 2409.07429) already runs an offline variant in which workflows induced from the whole training set are placed statically in the prompt with no per-instance retrieval, and reports it competitive with the online retrieval variant on web agents. That is arm C and prediction 3 already executed, in a different environment, and the proposal presents the compiled-static arm as its risky non-obvious claim while never citing it. (2) MIPROv2 (Opsahl-Ong et al., arXiv 2406.11695) is the canonical study of instructions and bootstrapped demonstrations as two containers optimized against the same trainset, and reports that the demonstration slot often carries most of the gain; that is the prior for the substitution question, and it points the opposite way from prediction 1. Also, ExpeL itself ablates distilled insights against retrieved raw trajectories, which is most of prediction 7 already. MemDelta, the only collision the proposal engages with, is genuinely a different confound and is handled correctly; the danger is on the prompt-optimization side, which the check never searched.
strongest_objection: The matched-information constraint does not do the work claimed for it, because information is matched but optimization pressure is not. I1 is produced by 300 scored rollouts of hill-climbing with validation-guided candidate selection across 3 seeds; B is produced by a single non-iterated distillation pass over 500 episodes with no validation-guided curation, pruning, or best-of-N selection. So cell 6 minus cell 5 compares a searched artifact against an unsearched one, and the headline S >= 0.6 is fully explained by search beats no search, which says nothing about containers and which no memory-systems author would accept as a fair test of their system. The iso-cost curve does not repair this: growing the bank with more episodes at fixed distillation is not optimizing the bank. Second, and nearly as damaging, the precheck gate is a selection-on-noise device: a bank that fails is enriched until it clears +10 points on a 150-instance dev split, where the sampling SE of a paired gain is roughly 4 points, so the surviving bank is selected for upward noise; that inflates the denominator of S while the numerator is not similarly selected, biasing S toward 1 in exactly the direction predicted, with no stopping rule, no pre-registered enrichment budget, and no compute line for the enrichment loop. Third, the design cannot confirm its own prediction 3: the stated single-pair MDE is ~4 points and the proposal commits to reporting sub-MDE differences as inconclusive, yet prediction 3 asserts a difference under 2 points with no equivalence test specified. Under the proposal's own decision rule prediction 3 can be refuted but never confirmed, and TOST at plus-or-minus 2 points would need several times n=600.
what_would_fix_it: Add a memory-side optimization arm so the comparison is symmetric: curate the bank against the same 150-instance dev split with a call budget matched to GEPA's 300 rollouts (validation-guided pruning, best-of-N banks, or ReasoningBank-style self-judged refinement), and report S against both the naive and the optimized bank. Replace enrich-until-pass with a pre-registered bank plus a pre-registered enrichment budget, compute the gate on a split disjoint from the one used for the S denominator, and report S for the pre-registered bank whether or not it clears 10 points. Titrate B-dup so its I0 gain lands near the same 10-point regime as the real bank, otherwise the positive control lives in an effect-size regime where no ceiling or headroom argument bites and it cannot license the null-is-a-finding claim at the effect size that matters. Add a headroom control (an instruction that matches I1's accuracy but is built from information other than the training episodes, for example GEPA on a disjoint task pool), since I3 controls verbosity only and diminishing returns at higher baseline accuracy is a complete alternative explanation for a high S. Restate prediction 3 as a formal equivalence test with its own power calculation, or as a one-sided bound. Finally, cite and ideally replicate Agent Workflow Memory's offline setting as the precedent for arm C, and reconcile the +10 gate with the track's own prior finding that this bank fixed zero items and broke six or seven.
missing_baseline: An optimized-memory arm: a bank curated or selected against the same dev split under a call budget matched to GEPA's rollouts, so that the study compares optimized instruction against optimized memory rather than optimized instruction against a one-pass distillation. Secondary and also absent: an accuracy-matched instruction control derived from information other than the training episodes, needed to separate substitution from ordinary diminishing returns at a higher baseline; I3 pads length but not accuracy.
preprint_collision: The check is unusually candid and partly credible: it names MemDelta as a partial collision on framing, correctly argues that MemDelta's confound is inside the retrieval pipeline rather than a rival container, and it retracts five citations from an earlier draft as unverifiable. But candor is not coverage, and the check is one-sided. Every search it reports is on the memory-audit side; it never searched the prompt-optimization side, which is where the real collision sits, and it therefore misses Agent Workflow Memory (arXiv 2409.07429), whose offline whole-corpus workflow induction with no per-instance retrieval is essentially arm C and largely anticipates prediction 3, and MIPROv2 (arXiv 2406.11695), the standing prior on instruction-versus-demonstration substitutability. It also concedes it could not sweep OpenReview 2026 and cannot verify TERMS-Bench, which it itself identifies as the closest structural precedent for the central logical move of using a prompt optimizer as the control for a non-prompt intervention. A further problem for a reviewer: the entire related-work section rests on 2026 arXiv identifiers (2606.29914, 2601.22964, 2603.18272, 2605.21768, 2603.02473) that cannot be checked from the submission, and the admission that a previous draft cited five works that do not appear to exist lowers confidence in the remainder. The check is above average for this venue but it has not established novelty on the axis where novelty is actually at risk.
